articles.title: Did ex-BuCor chief Bantag just evade arrest in Ifugao operation?
articles.summary: Mayor Mariano Buyagawan Jr. says police received information that former Bureau of Corrections chief Gerald Bantag was posing as a poultry worker in Lamut, Ifugao

blocks.text: ARREST. Lamut police launch an operation to arrest former BuCor chief Gerald Bantag, a fugitive wanted over the killings of broadcaster Percy Lapid and inmate Jun Villamor.
Photo from Lamut Mayor Mariano Buyagawan Jr.u2019s Facebook page.
Mayor Mariano Buyagawan Jr. says police received information that former Bureau of Corrections chief Gerald Bantag was posing as a poultry worker in Lamut, Ifugao

items: Former Bureau of Corrections chief Gerald Bantag evaded arrest during a police operation at a poultry farm in Ifugao on November 1, despite being wanted for the murders of broadcaster Percival Mabasa and inmate Cristito Villamor.
Mayor Mariano Buyagawan expressed disappointment over the failed operation, having hoped for Bantag's arrest and even prepared for a photo opportunity with him.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Former Bureau of Corrections chief Gerald Bantag reportedly evaded arrest during a predawn police operation at a poultry farm in Lamut, Ifugao, on All Saints’ Day, November 1, according to Mayor Mariano Buyagawan Jr.
In a Facebook post, Buyagawan said police received confidential information that Bantag was posing as a poultry worker at Sitio Alupapan in Barangay Pugol.

The Lamut Municipal Police Station launched an operation to arrest at 5 am Bantag, who has been a fugitive since courts issued warrants against him in connection with the killings of broadcaster Percival “Percy Lapid” Mabasa and New Bilibid Prison inmate Cristito “Jun” Villamor.
But Bantag was no longer at the poultry farm when police arrived, the mayor said.

Buyagawan said he waited anxiously at home for updates, hoping police would report Bantag’s arrest. He had even prepared for a photo opportunity with the handcuffed fugitive and planned to invite Bantag to be a godfather at an upcoming event.
“Wala na si General (The General is gone),” Buyagawan wrote, expressing his disappointment after police failed to find the former official.
Despite the unsuccessful operation, the mayor praised the Lamut police for acting on the intelligence report and pursuing Bantag.
He also expressed relief that no one was hurt during the operation, which he had hoped would end peacefully on a day traditionally devoted to remembering the dead.

Buyagawan joked that Bantag’s reported presence in Lamut showed that the town was peaceful and attractive, even to a fugitive. He also joked that former Philippine National Police chief and Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa might turn up in Barangay Mabato-Bato.
The mayor’s account did not explain how Bantag left the poultry farm or say whether police had verified that he was there.
Bantag has been wanted since 2023, when courts issued arrest warrants against him and former BuCor deputy security officer Ricardo Zulueta.

The Department of Justice indicted the two men in connection with Mabasa’s killing on October 3, 2022, and Villamor’s death on October 18, 2022. Mabasa was a radio broadcaster known for his critical commentaries, while Villamor was an inmate allegedly linked to the killing.

Mabasa was shot dead in Las Piñas City while on his way home. Villamor died inside the New Bilibid Prison in Muntinlupa City, days after a self-confessed gunman identified him as the alleged middleman in the broadcaster’s killing.
Bantag has denied involvement in the killings, describing the accusations against him as fabricated.
In 2024, the Court of Appeals rejected Bantag’s challenge to the murder case and arrest warrant in connection with Mabasa’s killing, allowing the case to proceed.
Bantag remains at large. A Muntinlupa court archived the murder case involving Villamor’s death pending his arrest.
Buyagawan ended his post by urging the public to remember the Lamut police officers who pursued the operation and making a tongue-in-cheek appeal for prayers for Bantag.
“Today is All Saints’ Day,” the mayor wrote. “No matter how you hide as a poultry boy, you are not yet a saint. You are still a fugitive.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Lacson: Majority bloc backs purging 'pork' in 2027 budget
articles.summary: The majority bloc is supporting efforts to remove questionable allocations from the proposed 2027 budget and ensure transparency in the budget-making process, Senator Panfilo Lacson said Sunday.

blocks.text: Published November 1, 2026 3:18pm
The majority bloc is supporting efforts to remove questionable allocations from the proposed 2027 budget and ensure transparency in the budget-making process, Senator Panfilo Lacson said Sunday.

“The majority of senators are rallying behind Senate Finance Committee Chairman JV Ejercito’s efforts to cleanse the 2027 budget of unwarranted, whimsical, and corruption-prone items. — ALL MEANS ALL!” Lacson said in a statement.

According to Lacson, Senate finance committee chairman JV Ejercito secured a commitment from the Department of Public Works and Highways to remove infrastructure projects with incomplete documentation from the House-approved budget before the plenary debates begin if the agency fails to submit the required documents by November 3.
A Senate review found that the number of DPWH projects grew from 11,420 in the National Expenditure Program (NEP) to 16,244 in the House-transmitted General Appropriations Bill (GAB).
Lawmakers introduced 6,271 of the new projects without initial vetting by the executive branch, the senator said.

Lacson earlier said the Senate would scrutinize all increases in the DPWH allocation, including the budget for the Ilocos Norte 1st District, the congressional district represented by presidential son Sandro Marcos, which recorded the largest net increase.
The Senate will debate the budget bill after it resumes plenary sessions on Nov. 9.
Ejercito had said the plenary debates on the budget bill are expected to start on Nov. 23.
In early October, Ejercito questioned the reported realignment of around P206 billion in the House of Representatives’ version of the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027.

Among the funding reductions he flagged are budgets for foreign-assisted projects, the calamity fund, flood mitigation projects, health facility programs, immunization, right-of-way acquisition, and health promotion. —Mariel Celine Serquiña/RF, GMA News

articles.title: A portrait puts Cainta’s sepoy heritage in the spotlight
articles.summary: A large portrait of 61-year-old Generoso ‘Papay’ Sumulong now hangs at Museo Cainta, honoring the town’s sepoy heritage. But his story raises questions about how a community recognizes the people who…

blocks.text: CAINTA, Rizal – Ask residents of Barangay Sta. Rosa where to find “Papay, the sepoy,” and they can point you to P. Burgos Street, to an old-looking house just before an arch.

At lunchtime, 61-year-old Generoso “Papay” Sumulong carried a bowl of rice to a tiled bench across from his family’s house, one of the spots where neighbors gather to pass the time. After returning to the house, he was greeted by a little girl who wrapped her arms around his waist from behind and called him “Pappy.”

Sumulong said the nickname “Papay” was derived from Popeye the Sailor Man, the fictional sailor created by American cartoonist E.C. Segar, who first appeared in the newspaper comic strip Thimble Theatre in 1929.

Sumulong, meanwhile, has become a recognizable figure in his own community: a relative who once took his niece’s daughter to school on his bicycle, a neighbor whom people approach for directions, and a longtime performer in Cainta’s senakulo (Passion play).

Sumulong’s face now has another kind of public presence. A large portrait of Sumulong hangs on the second floor of Museo Cainta, where it forms part of the town’s effort to preserve its sepoy heritage.
Created by artist Joel Rocafort, the seven-by-5.5-foot artwork, titled Sepoy, depicts Sumulong using charcoal and turmeric.

In a Facebook post on September 8, Cainta Mayor Johnielle Keith “Kit” Nieto described the portrait as “isang mukha na kumatawan sa kasaysayan ng bayan natin” (a face that represents the history of our town).

Rocafort said the charcoal used to draw Sumulong’s face and the turmeric used to color his headcloth were materials associated with Cainta’s famous suman and other traditional rice cakes. His piece went on display on the second floor of Museo ng Cainta when the space opened to the public in early October.
The portrait drew praise from residents on Facebook, with some calling Sumulong a “buhay na alamat” (living legend) and others commending Rocafort for bringing local history into public view.

But among the congratulatory messages were calls for Sumulong to receive an award, pension, or financial assistance. Some commenters noted that he no longer had regular work and asked the local government to help with his daily expenses.
The response raises a question beyond the artwork itself: What does it mean to recognize the people who embody a town’s heritage, and what does that recognition look like beyond a museum display?
Cainta’s official history traces the town’s sepoy heritage to the British invasion of Manila in 1762, when British forces brought Indian soldiers known as sepoys.

According to the municipality’s website, some of the soldiers stayed in Cainta after the British withdrawal in 1764 and settled among the local population. Their descendants remain part of the town’s historical and cultural identity.

blocks.caption: HONOR. An exhibit at Museo Cainta explains the significance of May 31 as Araw ng mga Sepoy sa Cainta and shows a collage of residents descended from sepoys. Photo by Dominique Astucia/Rappler

blocks.text: The town has also formalized its recognition of this heritage. Museum exhibits cite Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 2025-51, which designates May 31 as Araw ng mga Sepoy sa Cainta (Day of the Sepoys in Cainta), in recognition of the community’s contributions to local culture and tradition.
For Barangay Sta. Rosa Chairman Richard dela Cruz, who said his own family traces its sepoy ancestry through his grandmother, Sumulong is a recognizable representative of that history.
“Sakto talaga ‘yung mukha niya (His face is absolutely perfect for it),” Dela Cruz said.
Older residents with similar features had died, he added, leaving Sumulong among the people who remain recognizable to the community.
Dela Cruz clarified, however, that Sumulong is not Cainta’s oldest living sepoy descendant. Other families in the municipality have older members, including people in their 80s and beyond.

blocks.caption: THE SEPOYS OF TODAY. The exhibit mentions Dela Cruz as one of the public servants with sepoy lineage. Photo by Dominique Astucia/Rappler

blocks.text: Sumulong said his grandmother told him about their family’s sepoy ancestry when he was a child. He could no longer recall many details about the family’s origins, explaining that older relatives knew more of the story.
For him, the connection to Cainta’s history is also expressed through performance.

He said he began participating in the senakulo in 1976 and helped establish Kabataang Walang Sindak (KWS), his first group, before joining The Romans Club. He described the performances as a panata (religious vow).

In her book Semana Santa: Senakulo at Penitensya sa Bayan ng Cainta, former Cainta mayor Atty. Maria Elenita “Elen” Nieto traces the town’s senakulo tradition to 1904, when residents of Barrio Dayap began staging the Passion play. Over time, the tradition developed into larger productions involving actors, musicians, artisans and production teams.

Dela Cruz said Sumulong was known for portraying the high priest Annas and the biblical figure Samuel. Photographs he shared with Rappler show the two men during a 2009 Lenten observance. Dela Cruz said Sumulong had been performing since his younger years.

blocks.caption: IN CHARACTER. Sumulong portrays Annas, a high priest involved in the biblical account of Jesus’ trial, during a senakulo performance. Photo courtesy of Richard dela Cruz

blocks.text: The barangay chairman and Sumulong became friends through The Romans Club, which also participates in Cainta’s Lenten religious observances.
Dela Cruz described their relationship as close, saying Sumulong supported him even before he became barangay chairman.

Despite his longstanding involvement in local traditions, Sumulong has no regular source of income. He previously took welding jobs, but said illness and health limitations have reduced the work he can do.
“Wala. Minsan, natatawag, nagwe-welding sa araw,” he said when asked about his livelihood.
(Nothing regular. Sometimes someone calls me to do welding work during the day.)
His niece, Evangeline Sumulong Jambalos, said he still accepts occasional jobs and helps the family when needed. She operates a small street food business in front of their house.

blocks.caption: STAGE ACTORS. A younger Sumulong and Dela Cruz pose with fellow members of The Romans Club in 2009. Photos courtesy of Richard dela Cruz

blocks.text: Jambalos recalled that Sumulong helped raise her daughter, taking her to and from school on his bicycle. He also helps with errands and arranging goods for the family’s business.
“Malaki rin naman ang naitulong niyan (He has also helped us a lot),” she said.

Jambalos said Sumulong sometimes receives money and food from relatives. A distant relative living abroad previously paid him to tend plants, and family members have contributed to his expenses when needed.
Jambalos recalled that she and her cousins pooled money to prepare a small celebration for Sumulong’s 60th birthday.
“Nung nalaman naming senior na [si Papay], sabi ko, ‘Sige, lalakad kaming magpipinsan.’ [Kasama] ‘yung mga pinsan namin sa Cogeo, pinag-ambagan namin,” she said.
(When we found out that Papay would be a senior citizen, I said, ‘Alright, us cousins ​​will take care of it.’ Together with our cousins ​​from Cogeo, we all chipped in.)
Sumulong lives in the family home with relatives from several generations. He never married, but remains part of a household where family members continue to rely on and look after one another.

The family was surprised when they learned that Sumulong’s image would be displayed at Museo Cainta. Jambalos said they had not known the municipality intended to exhibit the artwork until other people began telling them about it.
“Hindi naman niya kasi inakala [na] lalabas siya sa mga gano’n,” she said.
(He never expected to appear in something like that.)

She acknowledged the public calls for assistance, but said the family was not asking others to solicit help on Sumulong’s behalf. Any assistance, she said, should come from the initiative of those willing to provide it.
Sumulong was similarly noncommittal when asked whether he wanted particular assistance from the local government.
“Kung ano ang ibibigay nila. Wala na akong magagawa. Kung anong gusto nilang ibigay,” he said.
(Whatever they give. There is nothing I can do about it; whatever they choose to give.)
He added that he would accept whatever help was offered rather than demand a specific amount or form of support.
The calls for financial assistance have also raised questions about what benefits Sumulong may qualify for.

Sumulong said he had completed paperwork for assistance but was told he could receive benefits only at age 65. His niece, meanwhile, said the family understood that he was too young for the Expanded Centenarians Act cash gift, which is reserved for Filipinos reaching the milestone ages of 80, 85, 90, 95 and 100.

These are distinct from the broader benefits available to senior citizens. Republic Act No. 9994 defines a senior citizen as a resident Filipino aged 60 or older, although eligibility for particular forms of financial assistance depends on the program’s requirements.

For Sumulong’s family, recognition is not only about what the local government might provide. It is also reflected in the everyday ways Sumulong has contributed to their lives and the neighborhood he has called home since childhood.

For the municipality, his portrait offers a visible way to preserve a part of Cainta’s past. His decades in the senakulo also place him within a tradition sustained not only by museum displays but by people who continue to perform, organize, and pass their practices on to younger generations.

The portrait gives Cainta’s sepoy heritage a recognizable face. But as residents’ comments suggest, honoring a person’s place in history and supporting the person behind that history are separate questions. – Rappler.com
Dominique Astucia is a Rappler intern studying BA Journalism at the University of Santo Tomas.

articles.title: Bulgarians vote in highly polarized presidential runoff overshadowed by Ukraine war
articles.summary: Voters in Bulgaria are choosing between two candidates with vastly different views of the war in Ukraine and ties with Russia. The runoff comes after a record-low turnout in the first round.

image.caption: Bulgaria remains sharply divided over its ties with MoscowImage: Stoyan Nenov/REUTERS

blocks.text: Bulgarians on Sunday began voting in a highly contested presidential runoff following a tight race between the two main contenders last weekend.

The November 1 runoff pits two competing visions of Bulgaria against each other. Moscow-friendly incumbent Iliana Yotova opposes military aid to Ukraine, while former caretaker prime minister Andrey Gyurov is backed by the pro-Western opposition.
In last Sunday's first round, which saw voter turnout fall to a historic low, Yotova won with 34.76% of the vote, less than three percentage points ahead of Gyurov with 31.95%.

blocks.caption: Iliana Yotova (left) beat Andrey Gyurov (right) by a narrow margin in the first round on October 25, 2026Image: BGNES

blocks.text: Although Bulgaria's presidency has largely ceremonial duties, the president can appoint interim governments during political crises, serve as commander-in-chief of the armed forces, and veto legislation.
Ukraine war divides Bulgaria

The war in Ukraine has become a central issue in the election, with voters heading to the polls amid growing security concerns in the Black Sea, which borders Bulgaria, following a rise in drone attacks targeting commercial vessels.
How Russian aggression is shaping Bulgaria's presidential election
Yotova has presented herself as a "president of peace" who favors dialogue with Moscow.
In a TV debate before the runoff, Gyurov accused Yotova of avoiding direct criticism of Russia over the Black Sea attacks.
"Russia must stop its aggression so that the next steps can be taken. Let us name the country from which the threats are coming," he said.
In response, Yotova argued that "peace can come only through negotiations," and maintained that continued aid for Ukraine "leads only to more destruction and the deaths of many people on both sides."
Yotova vs Gyurov: Between Russia and the West

If elected, Yotova is expected to pursue a similar approach to Prime Minister Rumen Radev — keeping Bulgaria on its European path while seeking closer ties with Russia and advocating the lifting of sanctions.

blocks.caption: A victory would make Yotova the first woman to be elected president of Bulgaria [FILE: October 25, 2026]Image: Valentina Petrova/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Her opponent Gyurov previously served as deputy governor of Bulgaria's central bank and as caretaker prime minister, leading the country in early 2026.
He has repeatedly voiced strong support for Ukraine and signed a security cooperation agreement with Kyiv during his premiership.
After the first round of voting, Gyurov said that Bulgaria faced a choice "between two personalities, two directions, and two ways of exercising presidential powers."

articles.title: Unbeaten Martin clinches world crown with stunner over Picasso
articles.summary: Tagged as a huge underdog, Ifugao boxer Carl Jammes Martin captures the WBC Silver featherweight crown with a split-decision win over Mexican David Picasso

blocks.text: HIT. Filipino boxer Carl Jammes Martin throws a punch against Mexican David Picasso during their WBC Silver featherweight bout in Saudi Arabia on October 31.
CANELO PROMOTIONS
Tagged as a huge underdog, Ifugao boxer Carl Jammes Martin captures the WBC Silver featherweight crown with a split-decision win over Mexican David Picasso

items: Carl Jammes Martin, also known as 'Wonderboy', won the WBC Silver featherweight title by defeating David Picasso via split decision in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
Despite being the underdog and facing a height and reach disadvantage, Martin showcased superior boxing skills and determination, even overcoming a flash knockdown during the fight.
With this victory, Martin is expected to rise in the rankings and attract more lucrative opportunities in future bouts, having trained intensively in the US prior to the fight.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Call Carl Jammes Martin “Wonderboy” no more. He is now a legit talent set to conquer the world stage.

Martin stunned touted Mexican David Picasso to clinch the WBC (World Boxing Council) Silver featherweight crown via split decision (96-93 and 95-94 for Martin, and 95-94 for Picasso) at the King’s Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday, October 31 (Sunday, November 1, Philippine time).

Defying pre-fight predictions and a 2-inch height and 5-inch reach disadvantage, Martin dictated the tempo of the 10-rounder, was the busier fighter, and landed the clearer power punches to beat Picasso despite incurring a flash knockdown, when his gloves touched the canvas after getting hit by a stiff jab in the seventh round.

Already the No. 1 contender by the WBO (World Boxing Organization) and the No. 7 by the IBF (International Boxing Federation) at super bantamweight, Martin is expected to enter the super featherweight top contenders after his successful foray in the 126-pound division.

Oddsmakers tagged Martin as the huge underdog because of the higher quality of opposition Picasso has faced, with one betting site assessing the Mexican’s chances of winning at 87% and Martin’s upset hopes at 13%.
Little did they know that Martin, true to his Lagawe, Ifugao, heritage, relishes the odds and thrives on challenges.

For three months, he trained hard with his father and coach, Abel Martin, before seeking help from United States-based trainer Marvin Somodio for the latter part of his preparation, starting at the Knucklehead Boxing Gym in Las Vegas, Nevada, owned by MP Promotions president Sean Gibbons.
Reaping the benefits, Martin dictated the tempo from the opening bell and outworked Picasso, leaving the Mexican no time to launch his vaunted body shots.
During the post-fight interview, Martin thanked the fans and said, “So much I appreciate this one (crown).”
According to Martin, he “learned a lot in the US, trained so much, and sparred with great fighters,” paving the way for the victory that left boxing pundits in awe and fight promoters on notice.
While Martin’s purse for the Picasso fight was reportedly at least $150,000 (P9.58 million), the big bucks would come on his next fight, wherever it may be. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Jacinda Ardern in Sydney Opera House talk advises politicians to ‘rebuild trust by building financial security’
articles.summary:
Former New Zealand prime minister has moved to Australia and is lecturing at University of Sydney – and from stage of city’s famous landmark

Jacinda Ardern, who now calls Sydney home, has…

blocks.text: Jacinda Ardern, who now calls Sydney home, has delivered a message to Australian politicians from the stage of the city’s Opera House.
Politicians, the former New Zealand prime minister turned academic told the audience on Sunday, were exacerbating the problem of polarisation within society and needed to be better.

“We have a responsibility not to engage in binary thinking, not to engage in the language of violence, [but] to rebuild trust by building financial security in a time of deep insecurity,” Ardern said during a forum with the author Anna Funder.
“There are things we could be doing but, right now, we’re making it worse, not better.”

In the past few decades, people across the world felt an increasing sense of insecurity as globalisation took hold, and they began attacking institutions like the World Trade Organization, Ardern said.
Politicians offered proposals such as Brexit in response to the insecurity – saying “Here’s what you blame” – which then paved the way for the rise of leaders like Donald Trump, she said.

The 46-year-old moved to Australia earlier this year. She purchased a house on the northern beaches in September and last week revealed she would be lecturing and mentoring at the University of Sydney.
Sunday’s talk was advertised as bringing together “two of the world’s leading thinkers” to discuss “can we disagree without becoming divided?”

“It’s not just that you hold a different opinion, it’s that you hold it so deeply that you have this view you’ve got moral clarity that is not being held by the other person,” Ardern said of the growing polarisation in public discourse.
“Therefore, you couldn’t possibly engage with them anymore. It’s made it much more difficult to create the discourse that we need to problem solve.”
Ardern and Funder were speaking a fortnight after the alleged attack on independent MP Helen Haines.
The former NZ PM did not mention the incident explicitly but stressed politicians and leaders needed to be aware of the tone they set.
Social media had made it more difficult for people to change their views, she told the audience.

“Your opinions are recorded and held in time, and when so much of a healthy democracy is your ability to have debate and shift your views based on new evidence of information … that environment makes it more difficult,” Ardern said.
When she entered politics in 2008, she was not only the youngest sitting MP in the New Zealand parliament, but also the first to enter with an existing social media account.
after newsletter promotion
At the time, many politicians – including Ardern – were excited to use social media to communicate directly with voters.
“I was so naive not to think about the fact that that meant the manipulation of information,” she said.
Her view of the online world changed on 15 March 2019 – the day of the Christchurch mosque shootings.

“A domestic terror attack came to our shores by someone who was radicalised on YouTube and who broadcast that mania in order to incite violence amongst other white supremacists using Facebook,” she said on Sunday. “That’s when I fully understood the weaponisation.”
Mistrust has been building for years and was now playing out in voters’ sense of grievance and insularity, Ardern said, adding politicians had not been able to address it.
“At every point where you see this spike in mistrust, you see this disruption in what people are feeling and experiencing, and a failure of a political response to it.
“We’ve not fixed the core of the problem; in fact, we’ve then weaponised it with blame and distrust of others. We have not just a crisis of trust; we have a crisis of leadership.”
Ardern suggested empathy was part of the solution.
“What empathy brings to politics is a thing that we’re missing now. It brings humility, it brings curiosity,” she said. “If we had more humility in politics – what a difference that would make.”

articles.title: Is spiritual warfare real? Exorcist explains
articles.summary: There is a battle that no one can see because it takes place in the spiritual realm, a priest said on Sunday.

blocks.text: Published November 1, 2026 2:26pm
There is a battle that no one can see because it takes place in the spiritual realm, a priest said on Sunday.

"Sa mundong ating ginagalawan, may nakikita at hindi nakikita. Sabi nga ni Saint Paul, ang pinaka matinding digmaan ay nangyayari sa hindi nakikita," said Fr. Ramon Unson Merino, an exorcist and parochial vicar of Saints Peter and Paul Parish in Makati, in an interview with Super Radyo dzBB.
(In the world we live in, there are things that are seen and unseen. As Saint Paul said, the most intense battle happens in the unseen [realm].)
Merino pointed out that the devil can affect people's lives in different ways.
He cited unexplained illnesses and sudden business failures as possible forms of what he described as oppression by the devil.

"May iba pa pong paraan kung saan tayo ay naapektuhan ng demonyo. Mayroon pong oppression, ito yung mga pangyayari sa ating buhay na napakahirap ipaliwanag tulad ng isang karamdaman na hindi ma-diagnose, yung magandang Negosyo na biglang bumagsak, oppression po 'yan," said Merino.

(There are other ways that we are affected by the devil. There is oppression, which refers to events in our lives that are very difficult to explain, such as an illness that cannot be diagnosed or a successful business that suddenly collapses.)
"Mayroon din pong obsession, yung ating minds na either the spirit puts negative things in our mind," he added.
Merino also warned of what he described as "openings" through which the devil could enter people's lives and potentially lead to possession.

"Yung occult is very popular in the Philippines, opening 'yan. Ikalawa, yung younger generation, lumalayo sa Diyos. Kapag lumayo kayo sa Diyos, ibang Espiritu ang papasok. Ikatlo, iba na yung takbo ng mundo ngayon. Yung mali ginagawang tama," he said.

(The occult is very popular in the Philippines, and that is an entry point. Second, the younger generation is straying from God. When you stray from God, a different spirit comes in. Third, the way the world works nowadays has changed. What is wrong is being made to look right.)
Unforgiveness and mortal sins could also provide openings for the devil's influence, he added.
As Filipino Catholics observe All Saints' Day, Merino said the intercession of saints could help people in their spiritual battles.
"Tayong naglalakbay sa lupang ito, pansamantala lang. Ang ating desire ay buhay na walang hanggan. Itong mga saints na ito ay magandang halimbawa," he said.
(We who are journeying on this earth are here only temporarily. Our desire is eternal life. These saints are great examples.)
"Taong-tao sila, may pagkukulang, may kahinaan, pero tumugon sila sa kagustuhan ng Diyos. Sa spiritual warfare, yung kanilang intercession ay very, very powerful," Merino added.
(They were human, with shortcomings and weaknesses, but they responded to God's will. In spiritual warfare, their intercession is very, very powerful.)— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Marcos Jr. visits father's tomb, sends flowers to Aquinos
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. visited his father's grave at the Libingan ng mga Bayani on All Saints' Day and sent flowers to the graves of Ninoy, Cory and Noynoy Aquino.

blocks.text: November 1, 2026 | 2:26pm
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. offers flowers the gravesite of his father during an All Saints' Day visit in a photo posted Nov. 1, 2026.
Marcos' office / Released
MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. visited his father's grave on All Saints' Day and sent flowers to members of the Aquino family, his family's longtime political rivals.
In a Facebook post on Sunday, November 1, Marcos was seen at the Libingan ng mga Bayani in Taguig City with his mother, former first lady Imelda Marcos.

Media reports said Marcos also sent flowers to the graves of former Sen. Benigno "Ninoy" Aquino Jr. and former presidents Corazon "Cory" Aquino and Benigno "Noynoy" Aquino III at the Manila Memorial Park in Parañaque City.
Ninoy was a leading opposition figure during the rule of Marcos' father, former President Ferdinand Marcos Sr.
His assassination at the Manila International Airport in 1983 helped galvanize opposition to the Marcos government.
Marcos Sr. was ousted during the 1986 People Power Revolution, which brought Ninoy's widow, Cory, to the presidency.
Marcos' visit to his father's grave and his flowers for the Aquinos came as Filipinos observed All Saints' Day.
Filipinos traditionally visit cemeteries on November 1 and 2 to remember departed loved ones.
Both All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day are special non-working days this year.

articles.title: Indian forces tighten security in Delhi ahead of big opposition protest
articles.summary:
Opposition says hundreds of thousands of people expected to participate in march demanding election chief resign over voter list changes

Indian security personnel carrying batons and shields…

blocks.text: Indian security personnel carrying batons and shields and accompanied by riot control vehicles surrounded the site of a planned opposition ⁠protest in Delhi on Sunday that is set to demand the resignation of the country’s election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists.

Authorities warned of traffic diversions ⁠ahead of the protest march ⁠and rally ​that will be led by Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi. The opposition says it expects hundreds of thousands of people to participate in what it says ⁠will be a major challenge to the prime minister, Narendra Modi, and his Bharatiya Janata party (BJP).

Opposition parties, student organisations and the youth-led Cockroach Janta party have held near-daily demonstrations since last month ⁠demanding that the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, step down over the voter list revision that critics say favours the ​BJP.

The Election Commission has denied favouring any ‌party and said wrongly deleted voters ‌can re-enrol, while the BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Analysts ‌say the youth protests, and growing support for the opposition, form the worst crisis for Modi since he came to power in 2014. But his government remains stable and the next general election is not due until 2029.
The opposition parties have announced they will hold a nearly 1.5km march on Sunday from central Delhi to the Ramlila Maidan, a ground that is the designated site for their protest ‌rally.

Visuals from news agency ANI showed riot control vehicles and dozens of security personnel armed with batons and shields outside the rally venue, where announcements were being made urging people ​to ensure smooth traffic movement and cooperate with police officials.

blocks.caption: Supporters of the Communist party of India (Marxist) walk towards Ramlila Maidan as they take part in the ‘Save Democracy’ march in Delhi.  Photograph: Anushree Fadnavis/Reuters

blocks.text: Delhi traffic police said a “large gathering” was expected at the venue, and traffic regulations and diversions would be implemented “as required”.

“People have started coming to participate in this rally ... we have ensured proper arrangements at the venue, and arrangements are also planned on the route of the march that will happen in ⁠a few hours from now,” senior police officer Rohit Rajbir told ANI.

The protests demanding ​Kumar’s resignation erupted after the Indian ​Express newspaper reported in September that ​his two deputies had raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and ​digital systems.
The change, which ‌began last year, removed ​over 130 million names from voter lists, including 28 million who died, 63 million who relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.

Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party – allegations the poll panel and BJP reject.

articles.title: Bolivia declares emergency as El Nino intensifies, threatens severe weather
articles.summary: President Rodrigo Paz warned of severe droughts and flooding as El Nino intensifies, with at least 78,000 families already affected by drought.

image.caption: The drought has already taken a toll on livelihoods and livestock in Bolivia [FILE: August 3, 2023]Image: CLAUDIA MORALES/REUTERS

blocks.text: Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz has declared a national state of emergency to mobilize resources and strengthen disaster response as the country braces for severe droughts and flooding linked to the El Nino weather phenomenon.
"This will be a phenomenon that will have very severe impacts in terms of drought and floods, and we need the cooperation of all institutions," Paz said.
Bolivia braces for extreme weather
The president's decree allows the deployment of additional rescue teams and calls for coordination between national and regional authorities, the armed forces and police.
According to a Bolivian government report, drought has:

items: affected at least 78,000 families across seven of Bolivia's nine departments
led to the loss of more than 75,000 cattle

blocks.text: Authorities have also warned of potential floods, flash floods, and landslides as the rainy season begins.
What is El Nino?
El Nino is a periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific that disrupts global weather patterns, often bringing drought to some regions and heavy rainfall to others.
The current El Nino developed in June and has strengthened rapidly since. It is now on course to become an exceptionally strong — sometimes called "super" — El Nino.
Researchers have estimated that the unusually high temperatures linked to the current El Nino could cause around 451,000 excess deaths worldwide from June 2026 to February 2027.

The United Nations has described the current El Nino, which is expected to peak in December, as "heading off the charts." Its impact could last years, with the UN urging nations in the Pacific to prepare for the worst.
Just in the past month, changing weather patterns associated with El Nino have been linked to:

items: forest and land wildfires in Indonesia
Supercharged Typhoon Champi in Taiwan
Hurricane Isaias in the US Gulf Coast
water and power shortages in India after weak monsoon

Alexandre Meneghini/Reuters

items: President Trump stated that Flavio Bolsonaro can remain in the US indefinitely after losing the Brazilian presidential election.
Bolsonaro left Brazil following a Supreme Court ruling that revoked his passport amid federal investigations, and he was admitted to the US under humanitarian parole.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated ongoing diplomatic discussions with Brazil, while Trump has no plans to support Bolsonaro's political ambitions.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
FLORIDA, USA – President Donald Trump said on Saturday evening, October 31, that defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro can stay in the United States indefinitely.

The comments, made to reporters during a Halloween party at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club in Florida, suggest that relations between the Western Hemisphere’s two largest democracies may remain strained for some time, even as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with Brazil’s top diplomat earlier in the day.

“He can stay here as long as he wants,” Trump said of Bolsonaro, who left Brazil after losing the election to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, despite leading in most opinion polls. “In my opinion, the election was a disgrace.”
The Brazilian embassy in Washington did not immediately return a request for comment.

Outside observers described the election as free and fair. Bolsonaro’s decision to go to the US followed a ruling by a Brazilian Supreme Court justice to revoke his passport shortly after his loss, as the candidate faces a pair of federal money-laundering probes in Brazil and police there considered him a flight risk.
He was admitted to the US under humanitarian parole, Reuters has previously reported, a status that typically only lasts for one year.
Rubio had said earlier on Saturday that he spoke with Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira at a Group of 20 meeting in Atlanta, and that they would see each other again in a few weeks.

In comments that had pointed to a potential rapprochement, Rubio told journalists that he and Vieira were expected to see each other again in France at a G7 foreign ministers’ summit that will take place next month. Brazil is expected to attend the meeting as an observer, he noted.

A US official and a person familiar with the matter have told Reuters that Trump has no current plans to support the political ambitions of Bolsonaro — who has described himself as Brazil’s rightful leader — despite allowing the Brazilian politician into the US. Trump on Saturday said he has no plans to meet with Bolsonaro.

Rubio said on Saturday that the US government “was not involved directly in any of the moves” that led to Bolsonaro’s departure from Brazil earlier this week. However, Reuters and several other media outlets have reported that Jason Miller, a White House official, helped arrange Bolsonaro’s journey.

Bolsonaro’s father, far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro, is imprisoned in ​Brazil for plotting a coup after losing his own re-election bid in 2022. Lula himself spent 17 months in jail in 2018 and 2019 on corruption charges that were later annulled. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Democrats are used to heartbreak in Texas - could Talarico turn the tide?
articles.summary: The state's $500m Senate race may be the most closely watched in the US midterms, and is about far more than control of Congress.

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Democrats hope James Talarico, 37, could end a decades-long winning streak for Republicans in Texas Senate races
By
North America correspondent

The race for a US Senate seat in Texas may prove crucial in determining which party controls Congress next year – a significant prize in its own right - but for both parties it represents so much more than that.

For the Democrats, their losing streak in statewide elections now stretches back more than three decades. In the second most populous state in America, liberals have been in the wilderness for a generation.
But polls suggest their candidate, 37-year-old James Talarico, may be on the verge of breaking through and turning a Texas Senate seat blue for the first time since 1988.
That would be a dream scenario for Democrats - and a potential nightmare for Republicans.

"If the Democrats do pull it off, I think it's going to cause a lot of soul searching and a lot of psychological damage to the Republican Party in Texas and nationwide," said Brendan Steinhauser, a Texas-based Republican campaign strategist.
These dramatic stakes help explain how this Senate race has rocketed to become the most expensive in US history, with total spending reaching more than half a billion dollars.
For Talarico, it has been a remarkable rise for a candidate who in 2025 was a relatively unknown state-level Democrat.

At the Fiesta Center in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday night, the line to see the softly spoken former teacher, who studied to be a Christian minister before entering politics, stretched around the building and down the wide parking lot to a busy road.

In this dusty western plains town of about 250,000, which voted overwhelmingly for President Donald Trump two years ago, a visit from a major Democratic candidate on the eve of an election was unusual.
"It's just so amazing to watch," said Aaron Gonzalez, the Democratic Party chair for Hockley County, which borders Lubbock. "This time is different."

blocks.caption: Supporters of Democratic candidate for US Senate from Texas James Talarico cheer as he speaks at a campaign rally

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters

When Talarico took the stage before an estimated 3,000 supporters – with another thousand listening on speakers outside - his pitch was a familiar one for many national Democrats this year, albeit with a Texas twist.

He railed against a conservative political establishment that he said is insensitive to the economic hardship of average Americans. He condemned the corrosive influence of big money in politics. And he promised to advance a "comprehensive anti-corruption agenda" in the Senate.
"Texans are ready for change," he said. "We are done with the extremism and the corruption. We're done with the politics of division, and we are ready for something new."

The slogan for his final two weeks of campaigning – "clear eyes, full hearts, can't lose" – is taken from Friday Night Lights, a popular early 2000s TV show about a plucky small-town Texas high school football team.

His music playlist leans heavily on twangy Texas country music. He celebrates Texas breakfast tacos, quotes legendary Texas singer-songwriter Lyle Lovett and frequently mentions that his ties to the state go back eight generations.

In the Lubbock audience, Andrew Robinson, a student from nearby Texas Tech University, liked what he heard. But the 26-year-old's optimism was tempered by an entire lifetime spent watching Democrats try, and fail, to get a toehold in the state.
"A Talarico win would mean so much," he said. "I haven't been keen on wanting to stay in Texas. And if the government were to change, it could give me a reason."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Donald Trump won Texas in the 2016, 2020 and 2024 presidential elections

blocks.text: Donald Trump won Texas in the 2016, 2020 and 2024 presidential elections
For Republicans, a Democratic win in Texas would have a very different meaning.

At roughly the same time Talarico was addressing his supporters in the Fiesta Center, Trump – alongside the Republican Party's Senate candidate Ken Paxton – was just a few miles away, in a venue twice the size.
"If you go out and vote, we're going to have a tremendous win in Texas," the president told the crowd.

Trump's visit to reliably-Republican Lubbock suggests the party is concerned about turnout even in the most conservative portions of the state. It is a worry that has been echoed by other Texas Republicans.
"Understand, we could lose Texas," Texas Senator Ted Cruz said in his podcast on Friday. "The Democrats are massively out-turning-out the Republicans."
Don Huffines, who is running for election as the state's chief financial officer, issued an even more dire warning. "Texas is the foundation of the Republican Party in America," he posted on X.
"When the foundation breaks, it all falls apart. When we lose Texas, we lose the USA."
For weeks now, party leaders have been warning that a liberal breakthrough in the Lone Star State could have dire consequences.

They fear a Talarico win would motivate more local Democrats to run for statewide and federal offices. Better quality candidates with more funding could lead to a snowball effect similar to the Democratic inroads seen in other southern states, such as Georgia, North Carolina and Virginia.
"I think that it's pretty clear that Republicans, especially candidates, consultants, operatives, and others who are active in the party, see that this is a real threat," said Steinhauser.
"The days of waving this off and saying that Texas would never turn blue are over."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Republican candidate Ken Paxton has a Trump endorsement - and some past controversies in Texas politics

blocks.text: Republican candidate Ken Paxton has a Trump endorsement - and some past controversies in Texas politics

For the Texas Senate race to come to the point where recent polls suggest Talarico has a slim but stable lead has required a unique confluence of events and political dynamics – a "perfect storm", in the words of Steinhauser.
"Everything that could go well for the Democrats is going well," he said, "and everything that could go badly for the Republicans is going badly."
But it is also a whirlwind that, in a significant part, has been sown over the past year by Trump himself.
The national environment for Republicans is a harsh one.
Voters are frustrated with high consumer costs, including the price of petrol, and largely blame Trump's tariff policies and the Iran war.

Political corruption has become an issue of growing concern. Democrats, independents and many Republicans in a recent Cook political report poll identified "greedy billionaires and corporations" and politicians seeking "personal gain" as the ones to blame.
What's at stake for Trump in the US midterms?
Texas-specific issues have also contributed to a hostile climate for the in-power party.

Polling and recent special elections in Texas indicate that Hispanic voters – many of whom switched to Trump to help him win the White House in 2024 – have soured on the administration's immigration enforcement policies.
Hispanics make up nearly a third of the state's population - and in more than a week of early voting in Texas, they have been casting ballots in historically large numbers.

Data centre construction, which Texas Republicans had touted as a welcome investment in the state, has drawn widespread criticism, particularly in rural areas that have traditionally been solidly conservative.

Texas Governor Greg Abbott, in his own tight re-election race, recently announced a one-year moratorium on AI construction in the state – a reflection of how quickly the issue has become a political liability.

"It's bad for Republicans," one Texas political strategist, who asked to remain anonymous, told the BBC. "We're asking a whole lot of the electorate at this point for us to continue to be the guys in charge."
Watch: Texas voters share concerns over cost of living ahead of midterms
Then there's the baggage that Paxton, who defeated longtime incumbent Senator John Cornyn in a contentious primary campaign earlier this year, brings to the race.

The 63-year-old Republican successfully painted the 74-year-old Cornyn as too old and too out-of-touch with Texas conservatives. He received a late boost, just days before his run-off election victory over Cornyn, in the form of a Trump endorsement.

"Ken Paxton has gone through a lot, in many cases, very unfairly, but he is a Fighter, and knows how to WIN," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Our Country needs Fighters, and also Loyalty to the Cause of Greatness."

The "a lot" the president referenced Paxton going through includes a 2015 federal indictment on charges of securities fraud – later dropped – and a 2023 impeachment by the Republican-controlled Texas House of Representatives on corruption, bribery and abuse of power charges.
The Texas Senate would later acquit Paxton after Trump intervened to pressure state Republican leaders.
All of this has meant that Paxton has more than a few critics – and enemies - in Texas, including within his own party.

items: GUIDE: What are the US midterms?
EXPLAINED: Why Trump's approval rating matters in the midterms
IN DEPTH: The Republicans walking a Trump tightrope

blocks.text: Talarico, by contrast, has proven to be an effective candidate. The state legislator defeated a well-known opponent, Dallas Congresswoman Jasmine Crockett, in the Democratic primary.

Since earning the nomination, he has maintained his polling lead despite a withering onslaught of negative advertising - much of it funded by the world's richest man Elon Musk, whose SpaceX company is based in Texas.
Musk alone has funnelled more than $170m into the race. Trump's MAGA Inc. committee has chipped in $40m.

While Paxton has proven to be an ineffective fundraiser, the third-party money spent on his behalf has blanketed the airwaves in the state – spilling over into sporting events involving Texas teams that air across the nation.

They have targeted Talarico for his past comments supporting transgender people, for calling "radicalised white men" a domestic terrorism threat and for criticising the fossil fuel and beef industries – two powerful interests in the state.
Talarico has distanced himself from some of those earlier comments, arguing many were taken out of context and "missed the mark" or were "deliberately provocative" or "cringy".

Meanwhile, the Texas Democrat has proven to be a historically successful fundraiser, amassing more than $140m in donations over the course of his campaign and setting a three-month fundraising record for a Senate candidate.

blocks.caption: Outside groups have boosted Paxton in Texas: A bar graph shows that outside groups have spent $220m on Paxton ads, with his own campaign spending $22m on ads. Meanwhile, outside groups have spent $83m on Talerico ads, and his campaign has spent $18m on ads

blocks.text: The funding has allowed Talarico to hit back at Paxton, highlighting his past controversies, and defending himself from Republican attacks.
He frequently leans into his religious upbringing – as the grandson of a Southern Baptist preacher who spent time in a seminary – leavening his stump speeches with biblical references.
There is one particular passage Talarico has been partial to of late – the familiar Old Testament showdown between scrappy David and the giant Goliath.

"We are going up against our own Goliaths," he said in Lubbock. "The billionaire mega-donors, the corporate special interests, the entire Washington DC establishment. Their power is real, but so is ours."

But the power of Texas Democrats has been overestimated in the past. In 2018, Congressman Beto O'Rourke posted his own historic fundraising numbers, generated serious national attention and ultimately lost to Texas Senator Cruz by just over 2%.

Talarico's polling lead, while stable, continues to rest near the margin of error in most surveys. And last-minute Republican appeals, as well as Trump's repeated campaign visits, could spur conservatives to turn out in greater numbers on election day, erasing any Democratic early voting advantages.
Inside the tiny Democratic Party office at a Talarico rally in Amarillo on Tuesday, retired schoolteacher Terri Mills listened to the candidate's stump speech.
Despite acknowledging the decades of Democratic futility and false dawns, she said she was allowing herself to hope for a Democratic victory once again.
"I have gotten my hopes up before, you know," she said. "But I do feel that this time is a little different."

MANILA, Philippines – Bacoor City Mayor Strike Revilla on Saturday, October 31, ordered the closure of a local pet crematorium after the remains of dogs and cats that were supposed to be cremated were found dumped in a vacant lot in San Jose del Monte City, Bulacan.

Revilla said the closure order against Ahjay Paws Aftercare Pet Crematorium had been implemented following a meeting with the crematorium’s owner, Jonathan Legaspi, and more than 30 pet owners who had entrusted their deceased animals to the business.
The San Jose del Monte City Police Station (SJDM CPS) earlier reported finding 25 dogs and cats inside seven large sacks near Barangay Minuyan Proper.
Residents reported a foul odor on October 31, while witnesses told police they had seen a white van and unidentified individuals unloading the sacks early on October 29.
Revilla said the crematorium had a valid business permit to provide cremation services in Bacoor. It operated two cremation machines, one in Bacoor and another reportedly in Caloocan.

Legaspi acknowledged that some pets had been taken to Caloocan for cremation. However, he could not provide sufficient documents or other evidence to establish that the cremations had actually taken place.
The owner also could not confirm if the animals found in the viral posts were among those entrusted to the business.
According to Revilla, the establishment had no CCTV footage or sufficient documentation to prove that the pets had been cremated or that the ashes returned to customers came from their animals.
The mayor said he had directed the city’s legal office, Business Permits and Licensing Department, Environment Service Department, and City Veterinary Office to investigate the establishment.

In a separate update on Saturday, the SJDM CPS said authorities had exhumed previously buried animal remains after pet owners sought to identify and retrieve their deceased pets. The operation recovered 16 dogs and two cats.

Police said unclaimed remains would be reburied at the Citrus Public Cemetery in San Jose del Monte because of decomposition and possible health risks. It was also coordinating with the city veterinary office and the City Environment and Natural Resources Office to investigate the disposal of the animals.
Rescue group Luna And Furry Siblings said all the recovered animals had been claimed by their owners.
It also called on the public to help gather CCTV footage, provide USB drives, and fund the printing of evidence as it prepares to file complaints.

The Bacoor City Police Station and Barangay Kaingin-Digman assisted pet owners in documenting their complaints, Revilla said. Some were seeking compensation and damages, while others planned to pursue cases with the police.

The Bacoor City Police Station is handling complaints for estafa and civil damages, while the San Jose del Monte police is handling complaints involving alleged violations of local sanitation and solid waste ordinances, according to the SJDM CPS.

The Philippine Animal Welfare Society (PAWS) condemned what it described as the alleged deception of pet owners who paid for cremation services, only to find that their animals’ remains had reportedly been dumped instead.

PAWS said the alleged acts may constitute estafa under the Revised Penal Code. It urged affected pet owners to preserve receipts, certificates, communications, photographs, and other records related to the service, and to seek legal assistance.
“The bond between a person and a companion animal does not end with death,” it said. “PAWS stands with affected pet parents in seeking truth, accountability, and justice.”
The Animal Kingdom Foundation also condemned the incident, saying the dogs and cats were not garbage but family members whose owners had paid to give them a dignified farewell.
The foundation described the disposal of the animals’ remains as an act of betrayal and a failure to value the trust placed in those entrusted with their care.
“Lahat sila ay inilaban ng kanilang mga pamilya hanggang sa huling hininga,” the group said. “At ng matalo sa laban ay ginastusan upang mabigyan ng maganda at marangal na pamamaalam.“

articles.title: C5 flyover repairs, road crashes disrupt Undas traffic
articles.summary: Several early-morning incidents occupied lanes along C5 as motorists marked All Saints' Day.

blocks.text: November 1, 2026 | 1:54pm

MANILA, Philippines — Motorists on C5 faced traffic disruptions on Sunday, November 1, as repairs continued on a major flyover in Quezon City and several road crashes were reported along the highway during the Undas weekend.

The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) began rehabilitating the northbound section of the C5 Boni Serrano Flyover at midnight on Saturday. The affected section is scheduled to reopen at 5 a.m. on Tuesday.
The work includes asphalt patching, lane marking, repainting of fences and installation of additional road delineators.
The DPWH has also installed steel grating to restore a previously closed drainage inlet and cleaned and repainted reflectorized delineators along the flyover.
The agency advised motorists to plan their trips and use alternative routes while the rehabilitation continues.
Slow-moving traffic, road incidents

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) reported slow-moving to moderate northbound traffic from the C5 Bagong Ilog Flyover to the service road on Sunday morning. Southbound traffic along the C5 service road was moderate.
Several incidents also affected portions of the highway earlier in the day.
At 6:06 a.m., two SUVs were involved in a crash on the northbound C5 Carlos P. Garcia Bridge, occupying one lane.
Another crash involving two motorcycles was reported at the C5-Ortigas IPI area eastbound at 5:50 a.m., also occupying one lane.
In Quezon City, a car crash at the C5 Katipunan-H. Ventura U-turn slot occupied one lane at 4:29 a.m.
Earlier, at 3:46 a.m., a wing van stalled because of a mechanical problem along northbound C5 Katipunan-H. Ventura, temporarily occupying another lane.
MMDA traffic enforcers responded to the crashes.

The incidents followed slow-moving traffic reported on Saturday evening along several C5 sections, including Eastwood to Bagong Ilog southbound, Palar to Bagong Ilog northbound, and Greenmeadows to Libis northbound.
In its 7 p.m. traffic bulletin on Saturday, the MMDA attributed congestion along those stretches to vehicle volume and ongoing DPWH roadworks.
Longer-term repairs in Pasig
Apart from the rehabilitation of the Boni Serrano Flyover, structural strengthening work is underway at the Pasig Boulevard-C5 Flyover in Barangay Bagong Ilog.
According to the Pasig City government, the DPWH project began July 11 and is expected to continue until April 5, 2027.
Work is scheduled daily from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. and from 11 p.m. to 4 a.m. the following day.
The city government previously warned that the project would affect traffic flow and advised motorists to consider alternative routes.
Undas travel preparations

The MMDA has deployed more than 2,000 personnel across Metro Manila to manage traffic and assist motorists near memorial parks as Filipinos observe All Saints' Day on November 1 and All Souls' Day on November 2.
The agency is also implementing traffic rerouting schemes around major cemeteries and crowded areas.
In Quezon City, local authorities warned of heavier traffic near cemeteries and memorial parks from Oct. 31 to Nov. 2 and advised motorists to use alternative routes.

Meanwhile, a moratorium on road excavation works across Metro Manila takes effect on November 1 and will last until Dececember 23, ahead of the Philippines' hosting of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit and the Christmas season.
The moratorium covers road reblocking, pipe laying, road upgrading and other excavation activities that could disrupt traffic.
The DPWH's scheduled C5 rehabilitation work is continuing during the Undas break despite the broader excavation moratorium.

articles.title: 2 vessels barred from sailing after Cagayan, Bohol mishaps
articles.summary: M/B Rose Marie 1 and MV Ocean Jet 788 are barred from operating pending safety inspections and technical assessments.

blocks.text: November 1, 2026 | 1:21pm
The fast craft MV OceanJet 788 as seen in a company promotional video posted in November 2022.
OceanJet

MANILA, Philippines — The Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) has ordered the immediate suspension of the safety certificates of motorized banca M/B Rose Marie 1 and fast craft MV Ocean Jet 788 following separate maritime incidents in Cagayan and Bohol.
In a statement on Sunday, November 1, the Department of Transportation (DOTr) said the incidents occurred on October 31.
The vessels are prohibited from operating while their certificates are suspended and must undergo safety inspections before they can be cleared as seaworthy.

Initial reports indicated that rough sea conditions and uncontrolled movement of livestock caused M/B Rose Marie 1 to partially submerge in waters between Dalupiri and Fuga islands in Cagayan at around 8:15 a.m.
All eight people aboard, including the captain, survived the incident. Six of the 11 livestock animals aboard died.
Hours later, at around 10:57 a.m., MV Ocean Jet 788 encountered an electrical failure while maneuvering to dock at the Port of Tagbilaran in Bohol.
According to the DOTr, the power disruption affected the vessel's bridge engine remote control and throttle system, temporarily compromising its maneuverability.
Both vessels remain barred from operations pending safety inspections and technical assessments by MARINA.

articles.title: VP Sara Duterte visits memorial for Super Typhoon Yolanda victims
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte paid respects to the victims of Super Typhoon Yolanda, which hit Tacloban City in 2013, a few days before All Saints' Day.

blocks.text: Published November 1, 2026 1:17pm
Vice President Sara Duterte paid respects to the victims of Super Typhoon Yolanda, which hit Tacloban City in 2013, a few days before All Saints' Day.

Duterte visited the Holy Cross Memorial Gardens on Friday where the victims of the calamity were laid to rest. She was joined by personnel of the Office of the Vice President-Eastern Visayas Satellite Office.
"Nag-alay tayo ng bulaklak at nagsindi ng mga kandila, kasabay ng ating mga panalangin para sa kapayapaan ng kanilang mga kaluluwa," she said in a Facebook post.
(We offered flowers and lit candles, along with our prayers for the peace of their souls.)
The vice president also encouraged the public to pray for the souls of those who died from calamities.

"Sa ating paggunita sa Araw ng mga Patay, isama natin sa ating mga panalangin ang mga kababayan nating biktima ng kalamidad at sakuna, gayundin ang kanilang mga naiwang pamilya," said Duterte. "Patuloy tayong maging matatag sa gitna ng mga pagsubok sa ating buhay."

(As we commemorate All Saints' Day, let us include in our prayers our fellow countrymen who were victims of calamities and disasters, as well as the families they left behind. Let us continue to stay strong amid the trials in our lives.)
Yolanda was the worst storm to hit the Philippines, with thousands of lives killed and 1.14 million houses damaged.
Roxas Night Market bombing victims
On October 30, Duterte also honored the lost lives in the Roxas Night Market bombing in Davao City last 2016, which killed more than 10 individuals.

"Binisita ko ang memorial ng ating mga kababayang nasawi sa pambobomba sa Roxas Night Market noong 2016. Sa banal na paggunita na ito, nag-alay tayo ng panalangin para sa kanilang mga kaluluwa. Nawa’y matagpuan nila ang walang hanggang kapayapaan sa piling ng ating mapagmahal na Maykapal," she said in another Facebook post.

(I visited the memorial of our fellow countrymen who perished in the Roxas Night Market bombing in 2016. In this holy commemoration, we offered prayers for their souls. May they find eternal peace in the presence of our loving Almighty.)
—Vince Angelo Ferreras/KG, GMA News

articles.title: Marcos visits dad, sends flowers to Cory, Noynoy on Undas
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. visited the tomb of his late father and namesake as the country observes the annual Undas in remembrance of departed loved ones.

blocks.text: Published November 1, 2026 12:13pm
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. visited the tomb of his late father and namesake as the country observes the annual Undas in remembrance of departed loved ones.
"Though they are no longer with us, the memories we shared and the values they taught us continue to bring our families closer together," he said in a Facebook post on Sunday, All Saints' Day.

In his post, the President can be seen together with his mother, former First Lady Imelda Marcos, and his younger sister, Irene Marcos as they paid their respect to their patriarch at the Libingan ng mga Bayani in Taguig City.

"Let us honor those who have passed not only through our prayers, but also through the way we care for those who remain. May these solemn days bring peace to those who mourn and remind us to cherish the people we hold dear," he said.
Aside from his father, Marcos also honored members of the Aquino family, including former presidents Corazon Aquino and Noynoy Aquino, as well as former senator Ninoy Aquino.
It must be noted that the Marcoses and the Aquinos were political rivals.
According to Super Radyo dzBB's Mao dela Cruz, Marcos sent flowers to the tombs of the departed Aquino members at Manila Memorial Park in Paranaque City.
Supporters of the Aquino family were also reportedly seen at the burial site to pay their respects.
In 2013, then President Noynoy Aquino said that he did not want to continue the revival of the Marcos family who at the time had assumed several political posts.
Marcos Jr. was a senator, the former first lady was a congresswoman, while Imee Marcos was a provincial governor.
But Marcos Jr. later said that the rivalry between their families is only limited to politics.

Kris Aquino, the youngest daughter of the assassinated senator and sister of the late president, recently shared that Marcos Jr.'s wife and First Lady Liza Marcos helped handle her annulment to basketball player James Yap in 2012. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: Marcos on Undas: Extend devotion to helping others

blocks.text: November 1, 2026 | 11:16am

PCO / Released
MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. called on Filipinos to extend the devotion shown during All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day to acts of kindness and concern for others.

In his Undas message, Marcos encouraged the public to draw inspiration from the selflessness of saints and the sacrifices of those who came before them, and to reflect these examples in how they care for one another.

"Across the country, families return to cemeteries, offering prayers and celebrating the lives and legacies of departed loved ones. Some travel great distances for these visits, finding an opportunity to reunite with relatives and recall the moments they once shared," Marcos said.
He said the memories of departed loved ones continue to strengthen the bonds of Filipino families and communities.
Marcos also urged Filipinos to extend the same care shown in honoring the departed to people who are struggling.
"If we can make time to revere those who have passed, we can also make room to listen to those who struggle, and let that same concern guide our society and the work of government," Marcos said.
He ended his message by wishing peace to those who mourn and reminding Filipinos to cherish those who remain.

articles.title: Trump grants visa to mother of Ghanaian boy killed in NYC — Mamdani
articles.summary: Javits Frimpong was killed on his way to school in the Bronx. He was 15 years old.

image.caption: Zohran Mamdani said he spoke with President Donald Trump on SaturdayImage: NDZ/STAR MAX/IPx/picture alliance

blocks.text: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Saturday that US President Donald Trump had agreed to grant a visa to the mother of a 15-year-old boy who was killed in a neighborhood in Bronx earlier this week.
Javits Frimpong moved to New York from Ghana last year to be with his father and begin a new life in the US, according to Representative Ritchie Torres, a Democrat from the Bronx.
Frimpong was shot in the abdomen on Thursday morning on his way to school and later died in the hospital, according to New York City police.
There have been no arrests in the case so far, with police investigating the shooting.
Mamdani says he spoke to Trump
"I just got off the phone with President Trump and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately," Mamdani posted on X.
"The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away," he wrote. "Javits Frimpong's mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person."
The killing led to an outpouring of grief in New York, with Torres writing, "Our entire borough is mourning a young man who should have had his whole future ahead of him."
The White House is yet to comment on the Trump-Mamdani phone call.
Teen was bullied in school, father says
Thomas Frimpong remembered his son as a quiet boy and said he was bullied in school by two boys.
Ghana's Foreign Minister Sam Okudzeto Ablakwa also thanked Mamdani and Trump in a post on X.
He said Ghanaian officials were coordinating with Javits Frimpong's mother to assist her with the visa application process.

articles.summary: Gabby Williams scored her team's final 11 points of the third quarter and dazzled through the fourth on the way to 30 points, and the Golden State Valkyries captured a championship in just their…

image.caption: Members of the Golden State Valkyries celebrate after defeating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday at Chase Center in San Francisco. (Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Basketball·Breaking

Gabby Williams scored her team's final 11 points of the third quarter and dazzled through the fourth on the way to 30 points, and the Golden State Valkyries captured a championship in just their second season by beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in a sensational first WNBA Finals Game 7 Saturday night in San Francisco.
Gabby Williams leads Golden State to 68-63 victory
· The Associated Press
· Posted: Oct 31, 2026 10:48 PM EDT | Last Updated: 11 minutes ago
Jordin Canada scored 18 points, Allisha Gray 16 and Angel Reese eight points and 12 rebounds for the Dream, denied another championship in the franchise's fourth try.
Gray made two free throws with 11 seconds left then Atlanta forced a jump ball — Gray against Williams — and Veronica Burton corralled it and converted two free throws with 5.1 seconds to go.

Rhyne Howard's layup tied it at 57 with 2:41 left only for Williams to answer once more by making a clutch three-pointer. She converted two free throws with 1:40 remaining, then Kiah Stokes scored a late basket. She pulled down 13 rebounds and blocked two more shots to cap her spectacular post-season.

items: Dream force Game 7 of WNBA Finals with convincing victory over Valkyries

blocks.text: Williams left Seattle with a great feeling about joining Golden State and its close-knit culture, returning to the Bay Area where she played youth basketball to build something special with the Valkyries — and she's now done that. Fans chanted "Gabby! Gabby!" throughout the fourth quarter.
When the final buzzer sounded, the violet-clad sellout crowd at Chase Center went into a frenzy as players sprinted onto the floor to hug and celebrate as confetti fell from the rafters.

"Ballhalla" had become "Boohalla" for this far-but-haunted Halloween night in the raucous arena. Now, with a women's championship to its name right alongside the one earned by the Golden State Warriors in 2022.

articles.summary:
Cryptocurrency exchange says withdrawals expected to resume on Sunday as FBI blames North Korean state-sponsored group TraderTraitor

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it has…

blocks.text: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance says it has replaced 90% of the ⁠amount stolen after a record $6.3bn hack of its platform by a group the FBI identified as being backed by North Korea.

The remaining 10% of tokens are less liquid, meaning they ⁠may take ​longer to buy, the company said in a post on X on Saturday. Co-CEO Richard Teng said separately that the company was “committed to covering the ⁠remaining 10%” and that “users will not bear the financial impact of this incident”.
Binance suspended user withdrawals after the hack, but said in its latest update that it was on track to resume them on Sunday.
The announcement came as the FBI on Saturday confirmed earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was behind the hack.

TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for The Interview, a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong-un.

“The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026,” the law enforcement agency said in a statement.

The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into Ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralised finance and instant swap services.
It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets”.

Teng said on Friday that the breach was a “complex attack” involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it ‌harder to trace and investigate.
Binance said it had set aside around $6.34bn of company funds to cover the losses.
“Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said.

The money spent re-buying tokens came from using part of its $1bn Secure Asset Fund for Users, a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches, as well as some ⁠of its Futures Insurance Fund, and the company’s own corporate treasury, it said ​on X.
The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.
Bitcoin plunged nearly 5% after the news of the hack, while Ethereum dropped nearly 6% and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10%.

The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea – which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programmes – to find illicit means to capture revenue.
